acceptance_criteria.criterion: getQueue() returns [] when the queue file or its parent directory does not exist.
pending + alive + no project → effective status is pending.
pending + alive + project exists → effective status is started.
pending + dead process + no project → effective status is dead.
pending + dead process + project exists → effective status is started.
started + synthesis_generated === true → entry excluded from result.
JSONL progress is resolved with correct human-readable summaries for each event type.
The queue file on disk is never modified by getQueue().

summary: Created mcp-server/gui/orchestrator-manager.ts with: RawQueueEntry / QueueEntry / EffectiveStatus types; QUEUE_FILENAME constant; getQueue() that reads the queue file, checks PID liveness via process.kill(pid,0), checks project-ledger.json existence + synthesis_generated, computes effectiveStatus, resolves JSONL progress, and excludes completed entries. formatProgressEntry() handles 11 JSONL event types.

comments.note: gui/orchestrator-manager.ts uses inline readFile() to check project-ledger.json rather than instantiating LedgerStore — avoids pulling in the storage layer and zod validation for a lightweight read path. Future WPs that also need LedgerStore methods may want to unify the pattern.

isProcessAlive() calls process.kill(pid, 0) with no platform guard. On Windows, process.kill(pid, 0) works correctly (returns true / throws) per Node.js docs, but this was not verified in tests. Consider adding a Windows CI note if the module is ever used in a Windows-hosted environment.
No observations beyond minor notes above — implementation in the newly created files is clean and consistent with the surrounding codebase conventions.

comments.note: isProcessAlive() catches all errors including EPERM (process exists but owned by another user) and returns false, treating a live foreign-owned process as dead. This is an inherent process.kill(pid,0) limitation, acceptable for a non-critical GUI monitoring feature, and was already flagged by the developer.
No observations beyond the EPERM note above — code is clean and consistent with the surrounding codebase conventions.

summary: Reviewed gui/orchestrator-manager.ts (new module, ~310 lines) and tests/gui/orchestrator-manager.test.ts (36 tests covering all 8 ACs).
Module documentation is excellent: header JSDoc covers queue file location, writer, read-only contract, and all 5 lifecycle transitions.
Fail-safe pattern is consistently applied: readQueueFile, getProjectLedgerStatus, and resolveProgress all return safe defaults on I/O/parse errors.

isProcessAlive(pid) uses process.kill(pid,0) zero-signal check; EPERM behaviour (treats live foreign-owned process as dead) is an inherent limitation, already flagged and accepted for this non-critical GUI feature.
getProjectLedgerStatus two-level fail-safe is correct: I/O error → exists:false; parse error → exists:true, synthesisGenerated:false.
formatProgressEntry switch covers all 11 JSONL event types + null for heartbeat + null default. Exhaustively tested with 18 pure unit tests.
resolveProgress walks backwards for last summarisable event; newest-file-first ordering via lexicographic sort on ISO-prefixed filenames is documented and correct.
getQueue uses Promise.all for parallel project-status + progress resolution per entry — good for latency.
One minor type-safety gap: isRawQueueEntry does not validate status === 'pending'. Downstream code ignores the raw status field entirely (uses effectiveStatus), so no runtime bug.
vi.spyOn(process,'kill') returns boolean in mocks but real signature is void — harmless since production code uses try/catch and ignores return value.
All 8 ACs covered. No blocking issues. PASS.

comments.note: isRawQueueEntry() does not validate that status === 'pending'. Entries from Python with unexpected status values would pass the guard. Since getQueue() ignores the raw status field entirely and computes effectiveStatus independently, this is not a runtime bug — but adding the status check would close the type-safety gap.
